correctness.rationale: The full quantifier-rank-three classification follows from: (i) the standard seven-point threshold in the three-round linear-order EF interval game, with explicit induction on remaining moves; (ii) two simultaneous coordinate strategies preserving product-order atomic relations, reducing all parameters to 28 cases; (iii) an exact, complete three-round atomic-type signature computed for all 28, with all 784 ordered pairs compared against the 21 canonical cases; and (iv) an independent literal three-round minimax cross-check of all 55 unordered pairs of small grids. The checker was executed from an actual saved file, and every finite iteration, including equality and incomparability patterns, is exhaustive. The 30-point minimum follows from the complete terminal-class parameter description, not a wider unproved statement.

value.rationale: The investigation solves a natural, complete quantitative finite-model-theory classification for the simplest nontrivial Cartesian products of finite chains, prompted by new work on chain-product theories. Its 21 exact classes, 25-versus-30-point boundary, and sharp minimal 5-by-6 terminal representative are mathematically intrinsic rather than arbitrary slices; all 28 reduced cases are closed, and the result provides canonical tests for bounded logical indistinguishability without needing a downstream theorem.
